questions.prompt: std::accumulate(v.begin(), v.end(), 0) is applied to a vector<double> {0.6, 0.7, 0.8}. What is the result?
questions.explanation: The init type decides the accumulator type: each partial sum is truncated back to int (0+0.6 -> 0, ...). Use 0.0.

questions.prompt: A std::set uses a comparator written as a <= b. What does the standard say?
options: It works but silently sorts the keys in descending order
It works only when the keys are integers, not floating point
Undefined behavior: the comparator must be a strict weak ordering
It works, but equal keys are stored twice in the tree
questions.explanation: With <=, comp(a,a) is true, which violates irreflexivity; the tree invariants can break.

questions.prompt: A sliding window of the latest 200 readings: push at the back, pop at the front. Which container fits best without extra bookkeeping?
questions.explanation: deque supports O(1) push_back and pop_front; erasing the front of a vector is O(n).

questions.prompt: After std::nth_element(v.begin(), v.begin()+k, v.end()), which is guaranteed?
options: The whole vector is fully sorted in ascending order, so every position is final and stable
Only v[k] is changed by the call; every other element stays exactly where it was before
v[0] is the minimum and v.back() is the maximum of the range after the call returns
v[k] is the element sorted order would put there; before it none is greater, after it none smaller
questions.explanation: It is a partial partition, expected O(n), enough for a median or percentile.

questions.prompt: A vector grows by factor g = 1.5 and 300,000 elements are pushed one by one. Using the bound g/(g-1)*n, what is the maximum number of elements moved during reallocations? Integer.
Samples (t=2.0, v=5.0) and (t=2.5, v=9.0) bracket the query t=2.2. What is the interpolated value? Give a number with 2 decimals.
A series has 100 samples at t = 0, 10, 20, ..., 990 ms. How many samples satisfy 250 <= t <= 600 (both ends inclusive)? Integer.
questions.explanation: The first is 260 and the last 600: (600-260)/10+1 = 35.

questions.prompt: A vector holds 40,000 samples of 24 bytes each. Inserting one sample into the exact middle moves the samples after it. How many bytes are moved? Integer.
A loop 'for (auto it = v.begin(); it != v.end(); ++it) if (bad(*it)) v.erase(it);' sometimes skips elements and sometimes crashes. Explain why and rewrite it in two correct ways.
rubric: erase invalidates the iterator and shifts later elements, so ++it is undefined and skips one.
Fix 1: it = v.erase(it) in the bad branch, ++it otherwise.

questions.prompt: Choose a container for caching the latest pose of each of about 50 tracked objects looked up by integer id, updated at 30 Hz. Justify, and say what would change your answer.
rubric: Proposes unordered_map<int,Pose> (or a vector indexed by id when ids are small and dense).
Notes that 50 elements make any choice cheap, so simplicity and clarity dominate.
Names a trigger for revisiting: needing ordered iteration, range queries, or millions of entries.

questions.prompt: Write the code that removes all negative values from std::vector<double> v and prints how many were removed, using the erase-remove idiom.
rubric: auto e = std::remove_if(v.begin(), v.end(), [](double x){ return x < 0; });
Computes removed = v.end() - e before erasing and calls v.erase(e, v.end()).
Mentions O(n) and that remove_if alone does not change size().
